judgments.reasoning_cat1: A list of authorization addressees on the exam form; the enumeration is long but the grant of authority is definite and the closing 'or employer' is a named category, not an open catch-all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reproduces the Part 1 authorization at c013 without differing in scope or duration.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The release-to-reinsurers clause with the 'unless required or permitted by law' exception; broad, but the operative permission and prohibition are both stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Identical in substance to c018 in the Part 1 authorization, so the two documents agree.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Twenty-four months from signing 'or while I have a claim, if longer' — an open-ended tail, but a workable one.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches c014 word for word, leaving nothing to reconcile.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A photocopy-as-original clause reduced to a fragment; the substance is a standard evidentiary equivalence.
The exam-form grant of authorization, adding 'or to its legal representatives'; the scope covers medical history, drugs, alcoholism and mental illness with the categories spelled out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to c013 and c017 and consistent with them in scope and purpose.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It describes the rider as allowing payment of a portion of the death proceeds before death and says accepting payment 'reduces the death benefit' the beneficiary will receive; how the reduction is computed is described only by cross-reference to a discounting formula, which is where such riders are usually fought over.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with the hypothetical illustration on the same form showing a $150,000 face reduced to $95,884 and with the $100,000 benefit amount in the Statement of Policy Cost, which use different figures for the same policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain negative disclosure that the benefit is not long-term-care or nursing-home coverage and may not cover bills; declaratory and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c026's description of the rider and with the 'No Charge' rider entry in the Statement of Policy Cost.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precatory suggestion to consult a tax advisor; it creates no obligation and nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It echoes the no-legal-or-tax-advice clause at c035 without conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Medicaid/SSI disclosure says mere ownership 'will not in and of itself' affect eligibility while also warning that receiving benefits may; the qualification is careful but the two halves point in opposite directions as read.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is a stand-alone regulatory disclosure with no counterpart elsewhere in the instrument to contradict it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A request that the policyholder review the policy and the attached application copy; hortatory, not operative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supports rather than conflicts with the incorporation language at c004 and c020.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The free-look notice states only that there is 'a limited number' of days to return the policy and refers the reader to the cover page for details, so the operative period is not stated in the provision at all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on a cover-page term not reproduced here, which leaves the actual right-to-return window unlocatable within the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Dividends, when applicable' are said to depend on investments and the current scale and are 'not guaranteed' — the 'when applicable' qualifier and the non-guarantee are the ambiguous edges of an otherwise descriptive passage.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The policy form itself is captioned a Renewable Term Life Insurance Policy, Nonparticipating, so a dividend provision sits awkwardly with the instrument's own characterisation of the contract.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The dividend-option text about buying paid-up additions or term insurance at 'current rates' which 'are not guaranteed' is descriptive illustration language, badly truncated but not carrying rival meanings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Like c032 it presupposes a participating policy, while the policy form is marked nonparticipating and the Plan of Insurance dividend boxes are unused.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line identification of the issuing company; the sentence is truncated but names a definite party.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The application header offers a checkbox between The Ohio National Life Insurance Company and Ohio National Life Assurance Corporation, so which entity is bound is fixed elsewhere rather than by this line.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A disclaimer that the company gives no legal or tax advice and a referral to the reader's own advisor; definite and unilateral in a way that raises no interpretive choice.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with c028 and with the illustration material without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'No one is authorized to make any representation concerning ... or change to your policy's risk class or rating' — an absolute negative whose reach over the company's own underwriters as well as agents is not delimited.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels the agent-authority limit at c010 and sits against the 'Preferred Nonsmoker' risk class actually assigned in the Statement of Policy Cost, which the clause purports to make unalterable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pointer to the Life Insurance Buyer's Guide for the meaning of the cost indices; informational only.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to an external guide not part of this instrument, but no operative right depends on it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A truncated note that values are affected by risk class and rating and that no presentation is made about future ratings; disclaiming rather than promising.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c036 and with the Risk Class entry in the Statement of Policy Cost.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Premiums may change annually thereafter' leaves both the trigger and the ceiling for change unstated in the provision itself, and 'may' does not say by whom or on what basis.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The policy form is titled 'Premiums Subject to Change ... Subject to Guaranteed Maximum Premiums' and the cost statement lists a fixed $132.00 first-year annual premium, so the interaction of the guarantee, the level period and annual re-rating is where a dispute would lie.
